readerValues.programmeDescription: Artificial Intelligence at the University of Amsterdam combines mathematics and computing with the study of cognition, language and how intelligent systems learn.

curriculum.limitation: Only the twelve first-year courses and practica (60 EC) are assessed. All 156 documented EC remain visible. The 96 EC of listed upper-year study, including 30 EC open space, are retained as published context but unassessed. The remaining 24 EC, final elective allowance, robot requirement and complete 2026-cohort pathway are unresolved.

componentNotes.y1-01: Studies functions, limits, derivatives, integrals and Taylor approximations, including functions of several variables.
componentNotes.y1-02: Examines major developments in information science and their historical, scientific and social significance.
componentNotes.y1-03: Develops academic writing, presenting, critical discussion, teamwork and reflection through assignments linked to first-year AI study.
componentNotes.y1-04: Introduces programming through functions, data structures, classes, implementation exercises and code review.
componentNotes.y1-05: Develops vectors, matrices, linear transformations, eigenvalue methods and least-squares modelling for AI.
componentNotes.y1-06: Introduces convexity, linear and integer programming, nonlinear optimization and selected search methods.
componentNotes.y1-07: Uses computational models of human learning and decision-making, including reinforcement learning and choice models implemented in Python.
componentNotes.y1-08: Develops probability distributions, estimation, simulation and Bayesian statistical reasoning.
componentNotes.y1-09: Continues academic writing and presentation practice, including literature research, a research proposal and a technical report.
componentNotes.y1-10: Develops symbolic AI problem solving through Prolog, recursion, state-space search and analysis of algorithms.
componentNotes.y1-11: Introduces learning from examples and experience, using mathematical and statistical foundations to develop and assess models.
componentNotes.y1-12: Examines AI safety, regulation, fairness, privacy, accountability and societal effects through discussion and group work.
componentNotes.y2-01: Develops neural-network principles and architectures, training and evaluation, including convolutional, recurrent and transformer models. Retained as published upper-year context; outside this comparison’s assessed first-year 60 EC.
componentNotes.y2-03: Develops communication, collaboration and professional exploration while helping students consider their third-year choices. Retained as published upper-year context; outside this comparison’s assessed first-year 60 EC.
componentNotes.y2-04: Develops statistical and neural models of language, their implementation and evaluation, and ethical questions about language technology. Retained as published upper-year context; outside this comparison’s assessed first-year 60 EC.
componentNotes.y2-06: Develops machine-learning pipelines, data processing, debugging, profiling, deployment and management of the model lifecycle. Retained as published upper-year context; outside this comparison’s assessed first-year 60 EC.
componentNotes.y2-07: Uses graphical models to represent uncertainty, infer relationships and learn parameters, with programming applications. Retained as published upper-year context; outside this comparison’s assessed first-year 60 EC.
componentNotes.y2-08: Develops data structures, algorithm design, complexity and correctness, with applications to AI problems. Retained as published upper-year context; outside this comparison’s assessed first-year 60 EC.
componentNotes.y2-09: Continues academic and career preparation through writing, professional interviews, reflection and application skills. Retained as published upper-year context; outside this comparison’s assessed first-year 60 EC.
componentNotes.y2-10: Develops computational models for image features, recognition, geometry and tracking, implemented in Python. Retained as published upper-year context; outside this comparison’s assessed first-year 60 EC.
componentNotes.y2-12: A small team develops and documents an AI project with an external company. Available projects and participating companies vary each year. Retained as published upper-year context; outside this comparison’s assessed first-year 60 EC.
componentNotes.y3-01: At least 30 EC of elective space is shared by the published schedules. The final allowance for September 2026 entrants remains unconfirmed. Retained as published upper-year context; outside this comparison’s assessed first-year 60 EC.
componentNotes.y3-02: Connects epistemology, philosophy of science, philosophy of mind and ethics to foundational questions about AI. Retained as published upper-year context; outside this comparison’s assessed first-year 60 EC.
componentNotes.y3-04: An individual supervised AI research project includes literature study, a method, implementation and evaluation, and a thesis in English. Entry requires completion of the first and second years. Retained as published upper-year context; outside this comparison’s assessed first-year 60 EC.

readerValues.comparisonExplanation: This comparison assesses only the confirmed 60 EC first-year Artificial Intelligence core for September 2026 entrants. UCR offers broader programmes combining mathematical and computational AI, learning agents, cognitive inquiry and ethics. Prolog programming, information-science history, the complete human cognitive-modelling syllabus and parts of the mathematical theory remain differences. The 96 EC shown from shared upper-year grids and the remaining 24 EC are excluded. At least 30 EC of genuine open study is displayed without assumed contents; complete degree progression and final research are not certified.
